issue_context.title: to_datetime errors='ignore' unexpected behavior
issue_context.body:
I'm trying to apply pd.to_datetime on an integer column to convert integers (including missing indicators) to datetimes. In order to preserve all the missing indicators, ideally, I would prefer setting the "errors" parameter to "ignore" to keep all the invalid parsings. But then I noticed that setting errors='ignore' not only preserved the missing indicators, but kept everything the same, even the dtype of the input column. See below for more details.  
 
```python
print(dt_col)
```
<Outputs>
0    20181223

1    20161017
2      -99998
3    20171220
4    20170511
Name: dt_col, dtype: int64
</Outputs>

```python
pd.to_datetime(dt_col, format='%Y%m%d', errors='ignore')
```
<Outputs>
0    20181223

1    20161017
2      -99998
3    20171220
4    20170511
Name: dt_col, dtype: int64

</Outputs>

```python
pd.to_datetime(dt_col, format='%Y%m%d', errors='coerce')
```
<Outputs>
0   2018-12-23

1   2016-10-17
2          NaT
3   2017-12-20
4   2017-05-11
Name: dt_col, dtype: datetime64[ns]

</Outputs>


Pandas version: 
- pandas==0.25.1

Is anyone else seeing the same behavior?
comments:
>  I would prefer setting the "errors" parameter to "ignore" to keep all the invalid parsings.

What's your expected output here? You can't have non-datetime64 values inside a datetime64 column.
That’s fair. I get your point. But I’m expecting at least the 0, 1, 3, 4-indexed integers being converted to date times, and -99998 can be left as-is. Is that something I should be anticipating?
This does seem a little counter intuitive so I think a bug. If you'd like to investigate would certainly take a PR to fix

not a bug this is doing exactly as advertised 
-99998 is not a valid date and hence not converted

we do not construct object arrays here (which would allow you to hold this value); this would be extremely inefficient

Hmm so is there any real point to ignore? I was expecting it to mimic what you would get from:

```python
In [32]: ser = pd.Series(["20181223", "-99998"])

In [33]: pd.to_datetime(ser, format="%Y%m%d", errors="coerce").fillna(ser)
Out[33]:
0    2018-12-23 00:00:00
1                 -99998
dtype: object
```

Instead of just returning the caller
It sounds like from the discussion that this is the expected behavior therefore closing. If there is further discussion on what the behavior should be we can reopen

review_comments: you added a ton of conditionals, i would expect that you can parameterize so that each is exercised (or simply not needed)
